body: “You Can See Everything,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, reached an impressive box office milestone this weekend, becoming one of the few documentaries to make more than $100 million worldwide.
Variety reports that almost all of the film’s $102.4 million box office has come from U.S. audiences, from whom it has grossed $93.4 million so far.

“You Can See Everything” will be opening in many more countries over the next few months — starting with Mexico, Brazil and Argentina on Nov. 25 and 26 — so its box office total could end up significantly higher.

And while the documentary was already an undeniable commercial success for indie studio A24 (especially with a reported budget of $7 million), it could now surpass the records set by the highest grossing documentaries of all time — “March of the Penguins” ($127 million globally) and “Fahrenheit 9/11” ($222 million globally).

articles.headline: Dem House leader Hakeem Jeffries refuses to rule out future impeachment attempts: ‘Hold the crooks accountable’
keyFacts: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries refused to rule out pursuing future impeachments against members of the Trump administration.
Jeffries stated that Democrats would prioritize lowering costs and investigating officials accused of corruption and wrongdoing.
Democrats are set to take control of both the House and the Senate in January with newly granted investigative and subpoena authority.
body: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries on Sunday refused to rule out trying to impeach members of President Trump’s administration when Democrats take control of Congress in January.

“We haven’t ruled anything in, and we haven’t ruled anything out,” the New York City pol told CBS’ Margaret Brennan on “Face the Nation” when asked whether impeachments would be an immediate priority for House Dems.

Jeffries, who is expected to become House speaker when the new Congress convenes, only said the Democrats would prioritize lowering costs for Americans while holding the Trump administration accountable for what he described as unprecedented corruption.

“We’ve promised the American people that, in addition to our affordability agenda, we know, in the face of the unprecedented corruption that has been unleashed on the American people and the country over the last two years, that we need to deal with accountability,” Jeffries said.
He said the Dems would investigate anyone accused of “stealing from the American people, screwing over the American people or shortchanging the American people.
“We will also hold the crooks accountable,” he said.
Jeffries added that any investigations would be guided by the evidence and the law.

“My expectation is that with respect to the accountability agenda that everyone involved and whatever investigations are unveiled, they’re going to follow the facts, they’re going to apply the law, they’re going to be guided by the Constitution, and they’re going to let the chips fall where they may,” he said.

Jeffries also outlined several priorities for Democrats when they take control of the House, including reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring some slashed food-stamp benefits, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and addressing the rising costs associated with Trump’s tariffs.
Democrats will rule the House with 257 members compared to 172 GOPers come January.
Hakeem also called for an end to the war with Iran, which he blamed for driving up gas, food and diesel prices.

The incoming speaker said Democrats would seek to ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks early in the new session, too, describing the move as part of the party’s broader accountability agenda.
Democrats’ return to power will give them greater investigative authority and subpoena power to scrutinize the Trump administration, setting up a potential clash with the White House.
The Dems also will take control of the Senate by 56 to 44 starting next year.

Trump was impeached twice during his first term, in 2019 and 2021 under Democratic control of the House, though the Senate acquitted him both times, with Republicans outnumbering the Dems in 2019 but not in 2021.

articles.headline: 'World's best could've lost 4-0' - but should Man Utd have done more at Anfield?
keyFacts: Manchester United lost 4-0 to Liverpool after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute.
Manager Mauricio Pochettino argued that even the world's best teams would struggle to avoid a heavy defeat under those specific circumstances.
Former player Roy Keane criticized the team's performance, stating that they should have shown more fight despite playing with ten men.
body: - Published

Mauricio Pochettino believes even the best team in the world could have conceded four goals at Liverpool in Manchester United's circumstances - but should the struggling Red Devils have done more in another disappointing defeat?

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager's first match in charge of United got off to a dreadful start as they had defender Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute and were 2-0 down by the 13th minute.
That left them with a mountain to climb, with Liverpool scoring twice more in the second half to secure a 4-0 win that kept United second from bottom in the table.
"Do you think that is easy?" said Pochettino of the situation that faced his new side after those disastrous opening 13 minutes.
"Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more. And now what we are going to say?
"We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing room."
'Do you down tools and throw the towel in?'
Pochettino certainly does have a point.

Trying to win any game when reduced to 10 men in the first half is difficult. In the entire history of the Premier League Manchester United have managed it on four occasions - each of those at Old Trafford.
Indeed, in the 509 instances of a team receiving one or more red cards in the first half of a Premier League match, they have gone on to win just 88 times.
At Anfield it gets even more difficult, with Arsenal the only team to have beaten Liverpool on their own ground after a first-half dismissal.
For ex-Manchester United captain Roy Keane, though, there are ways to lose if you have a man sent off - and a 4-0 defeat was not one of them.
Speaking before Pochettino's comments, he told Sky Sports: "Are you telling me they couldn't have done better? They lose 4-0 and everyone is saying it's not too bad.

"Has a team ever got a result before with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality. I can't believe what I'm hearing from people who have played for the club saying 4-0 is not too bad."
Keane was responding to his former team-mate Gary Neville, who was part of the commentary team for Sky Sports.

"That's where we've got to, where we're starting to write off 4-0 defeats at Anfield as though it's just the norm and what should be accepted," said Neville in the closing stages of the game. "The club's standards have dropped so far it's incredible."

The former England full-back added: "There'll be an element of, 'let's just forget about this game because Yoro got sent off, we've got 10 men and all that sort of stuff', but it rides into the game in midweek and from a defensive perspective I've never seen anything like this."
Keane did not agree with that view as he said: "Liverpool should have scored eight or nine. Unbelievable chances they had and everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad.

"I feel like swearing. I'll try not to. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad? Just because they went down to 10 men. That obviously made it a lot more difficult, but if you go down to 10 men is that it? Do you down tools and throw the towel in?"
'I've never seen anything like this' - defeat provides more defensive concern
Despite Keane's comments, a 4-0 loss at Anfield isn't unthinkable - certainly better than losing 7-0 as United did three years ago.
But in the wider context it provides more concern about a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe's top five leagues.
No other team in the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Ligue 1 or Serie A has conceded more than United's 34 goals in all competitions so far this season.
It is also the second successive game they have conceded four goals, while in their last six games in all competitions they have conceded 19.
"I don't think Mauricio Pochettino can write this off," said ex-Leeds and Spurs goalkeeper Paul Robinson on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"He has to learn from it. He will have learned about his players and their attitude.
"Liverpool had 27 shots in that game. There were mitigating circumstances early in the game... but why did we get to those circumstances?

"It was because defenders were out of position again. The long ball over the top that catches Matthijs de Ligt out, the lack of communication, the tackle Leny Yoro makes and the defenders being caught out."

articles.headline: Clayton says public should expect tech disruptions amid upgrades but remain ‘resilient’
keyFacts: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the public should expect ongoing service interruptions due to technology upgrades.
Clayton stated that cybersecurity threats are real and will continue, but noted the U.S. leads in technology and cybersecurity.
President Donald Trump and Clayton urged the public to relax and remain resilient in response to recent technological outages.
body: U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the public should continue to expect “glitches, gaps, and interruptions in service” as technology systems upgrade in the era of artificial intelligence .

Clayton appeared on CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday to address the series of outages and technological disruptions that have hit the U.S. throughout the past two weeks. In the wake of disruptions affecting systems such as Outlook, U.S. air traffic control, and banking giants, Clayton told the outlet these gaps are going to continue to occur because of AI model and computing updates.

“We are in a period of technological step change – both in terms of what people refer to as models, applications, and the like, and in computing power. And in that technological step change, our systems are going to need to be upgraded. They’re going to need to be upgraded for performance and for cybersecurity. And as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service. That is going to happen,” Clayton said.
The national intelligence director also told the outlet cybersecurity threats “are real” and are “going to continue.”

“The good news, the very good news, is we lead the world in both the technology, the compute, the models, the application, and in cybersecurity. And we’re going to need to continue to do that,” Clayton said.

Throughout the snowballing technological issues that have gripped the nation in the past two weeks, concerns among the public have flurried on social media, with some members of the public stockpiling water and canned food in preparation for a worst-case scenario.
However, President Donald Trump has called on the public to “relax,” telling stockpilers that “everything’s good” during his trip to China.
When asked if Americans should be stockpiling food, Clayton called the American people “resilient,” adding, “as we have this technological step change, we will handle it as a country.”

“America is the most amazing and resilient place, and we have been living with interruptions. Let’s give ourselves some credit. Let’s go back to COVID, other things, Americans fought their way through these terrible things in an incredibly resilient way,” Clayton said.
He clarified the current situation is “not at all” like the level of the Covid-19 lockdowns.

articles.headline: Netanyahu’s Likud, Eisenkot’s Yashar end coalition talks without deal
keyFacts: Talks between Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar to form a unity government ended without an agreement on Sunday.
The parties remained divided over who would lead the next government and whether far-right Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be included.
The two parties stated in a joint statement that they outlined their positions and would hold a follow-up meeting without providing a date.
body: Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.

Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.
The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.

In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.
Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.

Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.

Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.

However, Eisenkot has opposed a rotation, and Netanyahu has reportedly insisted on taking the premiership first, while Lieberman has ruled out joining any government that includes Netanyahu altogether.

If unity talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote in the Knesset for a minority government before Eisenkot’s mandate expires. It would rely on outside support from the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas.

articles.headline: Turkey: Thousands protest closure of critical media outlets
keyFacts: Thousands of people protested in Istanbul on Sunday against the closure of opposition-linked media outlets in Turkey.
The protests followed police raids, arrests of senior staff, and government takeovers of several television channels and news websites.
Halk TV journalists plan to continue broadcasting on a new YouTube channel after facing ongoing government crackdowns on press freedom.
body: Several thousand people in Istanbul took to the streets on Sunday to protest the closure of several opposition-linked media outlets in Turkey.
Protesters chanted, cheered, and whistled as they marched several kilometers through the city, calling for press freedom and freedom of expression.

They carried a huge banner that read: "We want freedom of thought, freedom of the press, and freedom for journalists." The protesters were also carrying placards that read, "The press cannot be silenced."
What sparked the protests?
Turkey's main opposition party, Yeni Parti, called for a protest just days after police raided Sozcu TV, one of the last opposition-aligned television channels.
Senior staff members were arrested during the raid. A government-appointed trustee was installed, and the TV company was placed under compulsory administration.
It was the third takeover in a year following similar actions against Tele1, Halk TV, Turkey's most-watched news channel, and the leading digital news website, T24.
Timur Soykan, a journalist who was briefly detained for criticizing the government, said that the government was doing everything in its power to silence journalists but was failing to do so.
Soykan asked the public to support Halk TV journalists, who plan to continue broadcasting on a new YouTube channel.
Increasing crackdown on critical media in Turkey
Over the past decade, press freedom has faced sustained pressure in the form of prosecutions, digital censorship, and government accusations that journalists are spreading "fake news."

In the last two months alone, Turkey has arrested several journalists for their reporting on a multibillion-dollar investment fund scandal. At least two of the journalists remain in pretrial detention.
According to the media rights group MLSA, twenty-five journalists are currently imprisoned in Turkey.
This year, Reporters Without Borders ranked Turkey 163rd out of 180 countries in its Press Freedom Index.

articles.headline: The cool phone camera trick that can test your remote control's battery
keyFacts: Users can check if a TV remote's battery is working by pointing a smartphone camera at the remote's infrared emitter and pressing a button.
A flashing purple light on the phone screen indicates the remote's batteries still have enough power.
Smartphones can also serve as virtual remote controls for televisions using built-in IR blasters or Wi-Fi companion apps.
body: The cool phone camera trick that can test your remote control's battery
Your phone camera is useful for more than just food pics.

Smartphones are capable of many impressive and useful feats, from capturing detailed images of objects as far away as the moon to serving as a key part of our home security systems. But smartphones are also useful for much more mundane tasks, such as helping us figure out whether our TV remote's batteries are dead.

When you press a button on your remote control, it sends that command to your TV using infrared light. While many modern televisions ship with Bluetooth remotes that support features like voice control, they may still rely on an infrared emitter for basic functions like turning the TV on or off. The emitter is located at the front of the remote. It's a tiny LED on the front of the remote that's usually easy to spot, although some modern remotes hide it behind a dark plastic window.

To test your battery, launch your phone's Camera app, point it at the front of your remote and press and hold a button while looking at your phone's screen. The remote's power button is probably best, since many Bluetooth remotes still use infrared for that command. If you see a flashing light, usually slightly purple, on the front of your remote, it means the batteries still have enough power.
Use your phone as a remote control instead

The camera trick also helps you check whether your remote control uses infrared or Bluetooth for other buttons. If you press, say, the volume control and don't see a flashing light, then that command uses Bluetooth. Now, while this is a pretty cool trick, it can't diagnose every remote control problem. For example, a damaged button might not register your presses at all, so you might not see the infrared emitter flash even if your remote's batteries are working perfectly fine.

If you don't want to deal with remote control issues, you may be able to use your phone instead. Certain Android phones have built-in IR blasters; if yours does, you can set it up as a virtual remote control for your TV using an IR remote app. Modern smart TV operating systems like Android TV and Fire OS also let you use your smartphone as a remote control, even if it doesn't feature an IR emitter. You'll need to install a companion app on your phone, log in to the same account as your TV and connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi network.

For example, the Google Home app works with smart TVs powered by Google TV and Android TV. You can navigate the user interface using D-pad controls, adjust the volume or search for movie titles faster using your phone's keyboard. articles.headline: ‘I feel like swearing’ – Roy Keane rages as he makes Man United pub team jibe
keyFacts: Roy Keane criticized Manchester United players as a pub team following their 4-0 loss to Liverpool.
The defeat occurred during Mauricio Pochettino’s first match as manager, leaving the club second from bottom in the Premier League.
Manchester United will next play Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday.
body: Roy Keane took aim at Manchester United’s players with a furious rant following their latest embarrassment.
The Red Devils succumbed to a heavy 4-0 defeat away against Liverpool on Sunday.
Keane slammed United’s performance against Liverpool as he questioned the fans for ‘applauding rubbish’ Getty
Mauricio Pochettino’s first match as manager also saw his side reduced to ten men after Leny Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes.
The result leaves United second from bottom in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 11 matches.
They are one point from safety after their winless run extended to nine fixtures.
Sunday’s defeat marks the first time ever the club has lost a Premier League match when starting the day inside the relegation zone.
View Tweet: https://t.co/fDwF2mJBBt
Meanwhile, it is the joint-heaviest loss by a United boss in their first match as manager.
Pochettino has equalled the record set be Lal Hilditch against Bolton Wanderers in October 1926, in a match which also ended 4-0.
Keane’s United rant
The result prompted a passionate response from former Red Devils captain Keane at full-time as he compared them to a ‘pub team’.

Speaking on Sky Sports’ coverage, he exclaimed: “If you do the basics right, you give yourself a bit of a chance so no matter how good you think you might be or a big club you are, if you’re not doing the basics right, you’re going to be constantly under pressure and constantly getting criticised.
“If that happened against a pub team, they’d be criticising you and this is a big game.
“You’re talking about starting well, being solid, but again, we go back to the defensive shape and one stray ball over the top puts somebody in on goal. It’s not good enough.”
United remain in the bottom three following their heavy defeat in Pochettino’s first match Getty
Keane was equally perplexed by the reaction of the travelling supporters to the United performance.
The players were applauded by their fans at the final whistle before heading down the tunnel.
Reacting to the incident, Keane said: “This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we’re talking.
“We’re blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?
“Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had.
“And everyone’s coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.”
Pochettino has equalled the heaviest defeat by a United boss in their first match as manager Getty
He continued: “Has a team ever got a result before with ten men? It can be done.
“Are you telling me Man United couldn’t have done better and everyone is saying it’s not bad. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality, I can’t believe what I’m hearing.
“Fans are applauding the players, applauding what? Applauding rubbish. When do the players take responsibility for some of the decision-making? Liverpool should have scored eight or nine.
“I feel like swearing. How can anyone say 4-0 is not too bad?”
The United players will have the chance to produce a response away to Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday, live on talkSPORT.
Pochettino then takes charge of his first home match on Saturday as Brentford visit Old Trafford.

articles.headline: Sorry, Vice City, but You’re the Most Boring Part of GTA 6
keyFacts: A Polygon writer argues that Vice City is the least interesting location in Grand Theft Auto 6.
The author claims the game's smaller towns and rural areas are more engaging than the neon-lit city environment.
The article highlights that diverse regions like the Leonida Keys and Lummox County offer more unique experiences than the familiar urban setting.
body: When Grand Theft Auto 6 was first announced, fans were thrilled at the prospect of returning to Vice City. The Miami-inspired location has always been one of the series’ most memorable locations, its neon-lit streets standing in contrast to the grittiness of Liberty City. While I was as excited as anyone to go clubbing and spend some time on the beach, after 70 hours, GTA 6 has struck me with one surprise thought: Vice City is the least interesting part of Leonida.

I don’t mean to say that Vice City sucks — far from it! It’s an immaculately designed video game city with more environmental diversity in any given corner than some open-world games fit into an entire map. The fact that it’s one of my least favorite places to spend time is more a testament to every other location in GTA 6’s Florida-inspired world. From small towns to the deep wilderness, every corner of Leonida is a delight to discover because every area feels so different.

I blame GTA 6’s opening chapter for spoiling me rotten. Jason and Lucia’s story begins in the Leonida Keys, a brilliantly constructed introductory area that I fell in love with instantly. As someone who is fascinated by the Florida Keys, the real islands that the location is based on, I was thrilled to find a digital space that so accurately captured a genuinely surreal part of America. The real Keys feel like an isolated nation, densely packing stores and suburbs onto narrow islands. The Leonida Keys feel both like an idyllic vacation hideaway and a mundane suburb, which gives GTA 6’s opening chapter such a distinct feel from the rest of the game. The small town nature of it makes for one of my favorite chunks of any GTA game.

Even after getting out of the Leonida Keys, it’s still a while before you get to Vice City. First, Jason and Lucia spend a stint upstate hopping around some small towns separated by vast farmland. Port Gellhorn has the feel of an industrial town, the kind of place that’s lined with used car lots. Some great action set pieces come out of that setup; one time I busted up a well-guarded abandoned bowling alley and wound up in a gritty gang shootout.

Way south of there, you’ll find Capri, another highlight. The squeaky-clean upper-class town is full of boutique clothing stores and high-end cafes. When Jason and Lucia arrive there, they are immediately profiled by street cops who clock them as poor outsiders who don’t belong in town. It stings considering how hard up for cash the two are when they get there, which turns the town itself into one of GTA 6’s greatest antagonists. Screw this place!

Even the stretches of map that seem empty at a glance are fascinating. Some of my favorite moments so far have been spent in Lummox County, which is largely made up of woods and mountains (despite IRL Florida not technically having those). Some of the best date spots and activities are up there, hidden alongside hiking trails. It’s also home to some true weirdos, like a group of “conservationist” gun nuts who say they are controlling the ecosystem by shooting at invasive lizards. Those weirdo discoveries make what could have been a dull, empty area into a place that I keep feeling compelled to bike around.

Between all of those areas, there are so many little pockets of the map to love. Hullet Marsh hides one of the game’s weirdest secrets amid the alligators. Tiny islands like Belpoint are quaint little escapes worth seeking out. Even unassuming stretches of road, like the area under Buckskin Swamp, will lead you to decaying mini-golf courses that make you feel like you’re in a state with a lot of history to it. I’ve seen every corner of the map, and very little of it has felt like a waste of exploration.

Vice City is excellent too, of course. It’s a perfect representation of Miami, right down to the hotel pools that I’ve sat by while visiting my brother, who lives there. Vice Beach is a highlight, and the various Keys around the city give the area a lot of diversity. It’s more just that I expected all of that. I know that Rockstar can get the hustle and bustle of cities right, because I’ve been playing GTA games since I was a kid. It’s more exciting to see GTA 6 branch out into more intimate towns and figure out how to make those just as exciting without the sports cars and nightclubs. GTA games have explored these spaces before, but the sheer mass of them here helps Leonida feel like a fully realized state with its own economic and political nuances from region to region.

My relationship to Vice City as it stands is similar to the relationship I have to Manhattan as a Brooklynite. It’s work island. Clock in, make some money, and leave the city limits at sunset to actually live a little. I’ll remember my mini-golf games more than the hours I spent sitting in traffic on Vice City’s freeways.

articles.headline: How to complete the Hyde Island Manhunt Easter egg in GTA 6
keyFacts: Players can trigger a manhunt Easter egg by traveling to the northern Hyde Island location in GTA 6.
To complete the challenge, players must defeat an armored hunter and his dog using limited ammunition found at outposts.
Defeating the hunter rewards players with the legendary Island Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle.
body: One of the many Easter eggs in GTA 6 involves you getting into a gruelling manhunt in Hyde Island. This is no ordinary foe, since he yields a might sniper rifle that can leave you wasted in just one shot.
To solve the challenge, you have to take the hunter down without dying in the process.
Table of contents
GTA 6 Manhunt Easter egg location
How to solve the Manhunt in GTA 6 Hyde Island
GTA 6 Manhunt Easter egg location
To solve this puzzle, we have to travel to the extreme right corner in the northern area of the map. There, you’ll find Hyde Island, located separately close to the mainland.

Screenshot by GTA 6 Bible. Remix by Destructoid When you try to get to the middle point of the location, you’ll get shot with a tranquilizer dart, and you’ll lose consciousness. When you wake up, you’ll find yourself in a container and a collar around your neck.
Screenshot by Destructoid Wait for the instructions, and then the container doors will open.
Make sure you go and check out our sister site, GTA 6 Bible , for all your GTA 6 needs.
How to solve the Manhunt in GTA 6 Hyde Island

You’ll find several outposts throughout the island that will feature a pistol and a shotgun. To complete the Manhunt, you need to take down the hunter and his dog. However, you can’t shoot them directly. Both of them wear bulletproof armor that protects them from shots. The hunter also has a powerful sniper that will do an incredible amount of damage.
Screenshot by Destructoid Finding weapons and ammo will be crucial, especially the latter. Ammo won’t be abundant, so you need to use it judiciously. First, kill the dog by shooting in the head.

Once the dog is dealt with, it becomes easier to kill the hunter. First, you always have to be on the move to avoid getting shot. Maintain distance from the hunter so that you can spare yourself from taking damage.
Once you have gathered at least six shotgun shells, close in. Two shells will knock him down, and you can then use the pistol to kill him.
Looting the hunter will get you the Island Poacher FF-50, which is the same legendary rifle he was using.

articles.headline: US intelligence chief says he trusts Trump’s description of Putin as ‘my friend’
keyFacts: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said he trusts Donald Trump after Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin a friend.
Trump's comments sparked criticism from United States lawmakers and foreign leaders who said Putin is a war criminal and adversary.
Clayton also stated that Americans should expect further technology outages as companies and government agencies replace aging systems.
body: Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China.

Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and posted a photo of himself and Putin shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”
On CNN’s State of the Union, Dana Bash asked Clayton whether he also thinks Putin is a friend to the US.

“The president is the greatest conductor of foreign policy in a very challenging time that we have seen,” said Clayton on Sunday. “Getting the three nuclear powers together and getting them to agree that they are not going to escalate, that they are going to communicate, that is historic. That is remarkable and, in that context, whatever language the president wants to use, I trust him completely.”
Bash pressed on whether Clayton personally agrees that Putin should be considered a friend.
“Dana, in different contexts, you can use different words. The president pulling off that summit, getting the three of them together, is just remarkable,” Clayton replied.
Speaking with ABC’s Jonathan Karl on This Week, Clayton made similar comments, saying that “using the term ‘friend’ is entirely appropriate” in the context of the summit.

“That conversation, that picture – historic, historic picture – was in the context of the three nuclear powers, the three main nuclear powers, getting together and saying, ‘We cannot have a nuclear incident,’” Clayton said on Sunday, referring to Trump’s post. “In that circle of that conversation, using the term ‘friend’ is entirely appropriate.”
Clayton also dodged when asked again whether he thinks Putin should be considered a friend to the United States.
“Is Vladimir Putin America’s friend? He is not America’s friend in Ukraine. Not at all. Not at all,” Clayton responded.
Last week, Trump sidestepped questions about his views on a friendship with Putin.
“I can’t speak to America,” Trump said in a press briefing. “I have fantastic relationships with Putin, that’s a very good thing.”
Trump’s characterization of Putin has sparked backlash from US lawmakers and officials abroad.

“Who is he? He’s the man who has abducted tens of thousands of children, killed tens of thousands of civilians, targeted civilian infrastructure across Ukraine, detained Americans wrongfully, and continues to do so daily,” Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer posted on social media.
“Embarrassing, despicable, and quite frankly pathetic,” Schumer added. “Senate Democrats will always stand with Ukraine and against Putin and autocratic dictators around the world.”
“It’s beyond me,” Senator Jeanne Shaheen said in an interview with MS NOW. “I don’t understand the president’s admiration and cozying up to Vladimir Putin, who is a war criminal.”
Trump’s comments also drew rebukes abroad, including from the deputy leader of the rightwing party Reform UK.

“It’s just wrong at every level … And it’s a grave mistake,” Richard Tice told Sky News. “He is not our friend, Putin. He is, as others have said, a murderous dictator. And no one is in any doubt about that.”
Trump’s description of Putin as a friend also drew criticism from European allies of Ukraine. “Mr Putin is not our friend and will never be,” the Polish prime minister Donald Tusk said.

Separately, Clayton also faced questions about the recent spate of technology outages across the US and said Americans should expect more disruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems.
“And as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service,” Clayton said on CNN’s State of the Union program. “That is going to happen.”
- Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.headline: Alcaraz puts Zverev in shade as world’s best beats No 1 for first ATP Finals title
keyFacts: Carlos Alcaraz defeated world No 1 Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 to win his first ATP Finals title.
Alcaraz became the fourth man in history to win all four grand slams and the ATP Finals.
Despite a thigh injury, Alcaraz finished his season on a 14-match winning streak by playing more efficiently.
body: The titles of ATP world No 1 and the best male tennis player in the world are carried by two different names. This has always been clear throughout this messy, injury-ravaged men’s season but it was underlined in the grand finale as Carlos Alcaraz ended his campaign with a statement victory, defeating the top-ranked player, Alexander Zverev, 6-2, 7-6 (7) to win the ATP Finals for the first time.

So much of Alcaraz’s fortunes this season were defined by the wrist injury that forced him out for four and a half months during the spring and summer. No matter, he still managed to tick the two most important items off his to-do list this year.

After starting 2026 by becoming the youngest man in history to earn the career grand slam, he is now, at 23, the fourth man to win all four grand slams and the ATP Finals. Despite his long absence, he has missed only two of the four majors and two of the nine Masters 1000 events: the Canadian Open and Shanghai Masters.

Faster indoor courts were previously viewed as the conditions that make Alcaraz most vulnerable. It is fair to say that this is no longer true. Alcaraz ends his year on a 14-match winning streak after triumphing on two of the fastest courts, Paris and Turin.

This victory is all the more impressive considering he picked up a thigh injury during his match on Wednesday against Daniil Medvedev. Although he kept on winning, the Spaniard has been more cautious with his peerless movement and his leg has been heavily taped. He has learned that he does not always need to throw himself around the court at 100% intensity, that he can actually conserve energy, play more efficiently and still defeat the best players in the world. That might just be the most worrying development for the rest of the field.

Until the final, Zverev’s tournament had served as another demonstration of his enormous yet freakishly consistent serve, with the German not dropping serve at all en oute to the final. However, the opening game immediately underscored how much better Alcaraz is than the rest of the top 10.
The Spaniard immediately generated three break points on Zverev’s serve. In Zverev’s second service game, Alcaraz landed ample returns, forced Zverev into baseline exchanges and broke to love.

For much of the match, Alcaraz completely outplayed Zverev from the baseline. His concerns surrounding his thigh problems have forced him to play even more offensively as usual, and he has struck the ball so sweetly for most of the tournament, but he was also incredibly smart. He peppered Zverev with ample slices and slower balls, drawing short balls from the German by arresting his rhythm, before unleashing in full. Alcaraz’s forehand, the best in the world, usually commands all the attention, but he struck his backhand incredibly well all match.

However, even for a player who has won so much at such a young age, he rarely makes things easy for himself. From 6-2, 4-2, Alcaraz began to spray unforced errors as he fell to 4-5, 0-30 on his serve in set two. Then, after recovering to lead 3-0 in the tie‑break, Alcaraz suddenly trailed by triple set point at 3-6.

During this stretch, Zverev served well, he forced the Spaniard to earn every point through his consistent defence and came up with improvisational solutions to Alcaraz’s drop shots and variation on some decisive moments. The Spaniard, however, was extremely poor.

Things may not often be straightforward for Alcaraz: his ability to play his best tennis when it most matters remains an astounding quality. To the surprise of nobody at all, he locked in, saved the three set points, earned a match point with a sickly sweet point-ending drop shot and then, without hesitation, he pounded a backhand down-the-line winner to close out the victory.

After ample discourse surrounding his credibility as the new No 1, which Zverev complained about during the Paris Masters, he did respond in the right way on the court here, reaching the final with wins against four top 10 opponents.

But there are levels to this game and the gap between Alcaraz and the rest of the field in Turin this year is vast. He ends his individual season by providing an unforgettable reminder of the excellence the sport had to go without for so long.

articles.headline: Rockstar Says Darts Were Cut From GTA 6 Because It Didn't Have 'Unlimited Money or Time' to Make It 'Feel Proper'
keyFacts: Rockstar Games excluded darts from GTA 6 because the development team lacked the time and resources to make the activity feel proper.
Studio head Rob Nelson stated that the team prioritizes high-quality, realistic mechanics for side activities rather than including every potential mini-game.
Rockstar chose to omit features that did not meet their internal standards for quality rather than including them in an unfinished state.
body: Rockstar Games crammed a lot of content into GTA 6 , but fan-favorite mini-games like darts and bowling didn't make the cut because the team didn't have "unlimited money or unlimited time" to do those activities justice.

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained why the studio chose to focus on some aspects of development and not others during an interview with VGC . As noted by the site, picking up a game of darts has proven to be a good pastime in games like GTA 5 and GTA Online, but in GTA 6, the standards were a bit higher.

From NPCs to the feel of motorized scooters, Leonida is Rockstar's most realistic playground yet. Every blade of grass was given special attention, and while pool was one game the team was able to fully realize, not everything panned out like they had hoped. Nelson said "darts was a contentious one" when talking about the decision to cut it from the game, explaining that it was left behind because the team didn't have the resources to do it right.

"Even we… you hear they have unlimited money or unlimited time, even we do not and so sometimes you just have to admit we are not going to be able to make this to the level we feel we need to," he said.

Nelson elaborated, saying that, starting with Red Dead Redemption 2, the team started to treat mini-games more like activities. In other words, bonuses like darts became less about being a diversion of Rockstar's open worlds and more of an extension of them. The goal is to make pool, darts, or any other activity feel like it's just as punchy and weighty for Jason and Lucia as it is in the real world.
Using GTA 6's in-game workouts as an example, he added, "You’re not just pushing a button; it mimics what weightlifting is."
"A lot of work [is needed] to get it tuned right," Nelson continued. "Darts is one we just didn’t get to."

Long story short, Rockstar just "didn't have the resources" to make it "feel proper." His thoughts on the matter – or any scenario where a mechanic or activity is cut – were summed up in one line: "It’s better not to do it than to do it and have it not be good enough."
GTA 6 is now the highest-rated game of all time . IGN gave it a 10/10 review .

For one of the better examples of the care the developers put into side activities, look no further than some of the games Jason has on his JoySystem . You can see how Rockstar pulled from real-world inspirations to create his character here .

articles.headline: Democrats clinch historic House majority as Chuck Hubbard defeats longtime GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx
keyFacts: Democrats secured a historic House majority in the midterm elections, reaching at least 258 seats according to The Associated Press.
Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated longtime Republican incumbent Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, cementing the majority.
Democrats also gained control of the Senate with 56 seats, and plan to launch investigations and roll back Republican policies when Congress convenes in January.
body: Democrats have stormed back into power in the House, securing the largest majority of any party since 1992 in a sweeping midterm victory that will reshape the balance of power in Washington and leave Republicans with significantly less influence over the chamber.

The victory was cemented after Democrat Chuck Hubbard was elected to the House from North Carolina, according to The Associated Press (AP). He defeated longtime Republican incumbent Rep. Virginia Foxx, who chaired the powerful House Rules Committee, which determines which bills reach the House floor for a vote.

With several general election results still being called, Democrats have picked up 44 seats so far, giving them at least 258 seats in the House, their largest majority in more than three decades, according to The AP.
STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE
Meanwhile, Republicans have been left with at least 173 seats.
Four House races remain undecided in Minnesota, Tennessee and two December runoffs in Louisiana, according to The AP.

The party's projected majority will surpass its post-election totals in every election since Bill Clinton first won the presidency in 1992, when Democrats secured 258 seats, the outlet said. The party's next-largest showing reportedly came in 2008, when Barack Obama was elected president and Democrats won 257 House seats.
The shift in the 435-member House will set the stage for a dramatic power struggle in Washington .
WHAT THE 2026 MIDTERM RESULTS MEAN FOR CAPITOL HILL
Democrats are also poised to take control of the Senate , where they secured a 56-seat majority in the 100-member chamber, their largest advantage in more than a decade.

Democrats scored some of their biggest victories in traditionally competitive states and Republican strongholds alike, including Texas, Georgia, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina.
BLUE WAVE NEARLY SWALLOWED SOME OF AMERICA'S REDDEST STATES AS ELECTION DATA EXPOSES GOP'S CLOSE CALLS

President Donald Trump will face a new legislative reality when the next Congress convenes in January, with Democrats preparing to launch a flurry of investigations targeting his administration and its Republican allies in Congress.

The party's 100-day agenda will also focus on rolling back Republican policies, with top priorities including reversing GOP Medicaid cuts and restoring Affordable Care Act tax credits that Republicans allowed to expire, The AP said.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding
keyFacts: Epic Games announced that Unreal Engine 6 will not include the Blueprints scripting system at launch.
The company plans to use AI to assist developers in converting existing Unreal Engine 5 projects to the new Verse-based architecture.
Epic Games executive Marcus Wassmer stated that AI advancements will help deliver the engine on time while meeting new design goals.
body: Unreal Engine 6 will not launch with the engine's long-standard Blueprints scripting system. The news came in a Friday, November 19 post on the Unreal Engine website, written by Epic Games executive vice president of development, Marcus Wassmer. Here's Wassmer's top-level summary from the post:
"UE6, including UE6 Early Access, won’t include Blueprints or the Actor Gameplay Framework. Gameplay will be built in Verse and on the new Scene Graph framework.

"In June, we said Blueprints and Actors would coexist in UE6 Early Access and 6.0, so UE5 projects could upgrade incrementally while the new Scene Graph framework matures. However, with recent advances in AI capability, we expect AI to massively help with converting UE5 projects to UE6, if not make that process fully automatic. That also means we can deliver UE6 on time (or sooner!) while meeting its design goals: a new data model, a Verse-first architecture, modularity, and AI operability."

Blueprints have not (and it appears, will not) be deprecated in Unreal Engine 5, and the company maintains that projects will still be easy to convert from UE5 to UE6. Wassmer cited a declining cost in AI task completion as one reason for this belief, as well as the team's ongoing, but apparently successful conversion of Fortnite's Blueprint library to UE6's Verse programming language through an AI-assisted process.

Blueprints are a widely-used feature of Unreal. Former Valve developer Chet Faliszek, an AI skeptic, has put out a vlog on the subject. Essentially, Faliszek argues that Blueprints (and features like them in other game engines) represent a middle ground between artistic and technical work, an introduction and skill builder for less technically-minded developers. Without them, such developers seemingly have to either learn Verse code, or integrate LLM prompting into their workflows.

"We made a new skill in the middle there, between normal and expert," Faliszek said of intermediate tools like Blueprints. "To lose that determinism from game design, and instead have to prompt AI—or write your own Verse … It's losing those tools that made all those designers and all those artists so powerful, to be able to do really powerful things and have access to really deep-down things, but in a safe way that the engineers can decide what that meant to them."

A dark horse game of the year candidate, the first-person RPG Queen's Domain, was made with Unreal Engine. I recently spoke to co-developer Eric Berger, who specialized in art and design alongside the more technically-focused Bradley Boothe, a relationship that rhymes with the ones Faliszek outlined in his video.

I spoke to Berger before seeing Epic's latest press release, but Berger already indicated that Unreal's AI pivot is prompting Freshly Baked Games to switch engines for its next project. I followed up with Berger about this Blueprint news, and the developer said that Blueprints were a major part of the workflow on Queen's Domain.

I'm a layman in game development, but I think Wassmer's post elides that there is a large qualitative difference between doing any work via LLM prompt versus the old-fashioned way—I don't like or want to use these tools, myself, and I don't think that's an unpopular stance. Commenter ZILtoid1991 on Faliszek's video compared the move to Apple removing headphone jacks on the iPhone, a comparison I find fruitful.
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

It was hugely unpopular at the time, and is still derided by enthusiasts, but it also worked. Other manufacturers copied Apple, and everybody has bluetooth headphones now—or Apple's own, proprietary Air Pods. But Apple had far less success trying something similar with its laptops: The lack of ports on late 2010s Macbooks proved disastrous, and Apple has since reintroduced more (and a wider variety of) ports on newer models of the popular line. I certainly have my own anti-AI, pro-headphone jack preferences, but we'll have to see how this plays out with the Unreal Engine.

Ted has been thinking about PC games and bothering anyone who would listen with his thoughts on them ever since he booted up his sister's copy of Neverwinter Nights on the family computer. He is obsessed with all things CRPG and CRPG-adjacent, but has also covered esports, modding, and rare game collecting. When he's not playing or writing about games, you can find Ted lifting weights on his back porch. You can follow Ted on Bluesky.

articles.headline: Godfather Of Cyberpunk Says He’s Never Played A Video Game, But Finds GTA 6 ‘Intriguing’
keyFacts: Cyberpunk author William Gibson stated he has never played a video game despite his work influencing the genre.
Gibson expressed interest in Grand Theft Auto VI after watching viral clips of the game online.
Gibson said he is intrigued by the texture and depth of the game clips but does not intend to learn how to play.
body: William Gibson, the science fiction author often credited for establishing the cyberpunk genre, took plenty of inspiration from video game culture in the ’70s and ’80s. Despite this, and the influence of works like Neuromancer has had on the medium, Gibson says he doesnât partake in the hobby, claiming this weekend that heâs never even played a video game. One game seems to be recapturing his interest, though, the forefather of virtual reality allured by viral Grand Theft Auto clips online.

“Iâve never played a video game in my life, but this thing [Grand Theft Auto] actually does [seem] interesting,” posted Gibson. “When I said that I found that clip of the new GTA interesting, I didnât mean that it made me interested in learning to play it, but interested in what it was that I found intriguing, in some mysterious way, in itsâ¦texture?â¦depth? I donât know.”

In the early â80s, William Gibson released Neuromancer, the first novel in his âSprawlâ series and an establishing work of cyberpunk literature. In it, hackers, mercenaries and ‘street samurai’ orchestrate a heist across cities, planets and virtual realities. Much of the nomenclature around the digital world and the notion of cyberspace come from his works. And much of that world was built through observing teens and drug peddlers looming around Vancouver arcades in the â70s, as well as the rapid transformation of computers from fridge-sized number crunchers to desktop work stations.

Despite changing video games forever, and games directly adapted from his works, Gibson hasnât participated in playing them. Replying to fans stunned heâs never given one a whirl, Gibson says itâs possible he tried Pong, âon a tabletop in a bar?â

Now, like thousands others, Gibson is hooked on amusing clips emerging out of Grand Theft Auto VI. The one kicking off the conversation featuring a boom barrier launching Jason like a catapult to Luciaâs embarrassment. This time from the comfort of homes and phones, people around the world are sitting backseat to endless streams of the new game. Even those who donât consider themselves players taken in by virtual birdwatchers and infrastructure fanatics.

“I was enthralled by this one streamer pretending to host a nature documentary while wandering around the wilderness of Leonida,” writes Defectorâs Brandy Jensen on being unexpectedly taken in by GTA streams. “I cheered as Jason is, for reasons that remain completely beyond me, rescued by a dog driving a jetski. I even found myself beguiled by the many ways a digitally rendered human body can react to getting hit by a basketball.”

If the early sales figures are true, Grand Theft Auto VI is the highest performing piece of media of all time. The ramifications of which are surreal to wrap your head around, regardless of being an eager fan or a cultural observer. It has even reeled in William Gibson, though heâs still figuring out the words to describe the phenomenon. And once he does, maybe itâll lay the groundwork for the next century of speculative dystopia.

The issues with Delta’s systems in Atlanta come just one week after an FAA outage led to a nationwide groundstop and thousands of canceled flights. According to The New York Times:
